PREMISE CORRECTION: the column is NOT left NOT NULL (IS_NULLABLE=YES throughout). The cause is MySQL 8's ALTER COLUMN ... DROP DEFAULT, which leaves even a nullable column with no default at all, so a strict-mode insert that omits it is refused; SET DEFAULT NULL stores NULL (measured by hand). Round 1 was validated on MariaDB 10.11, where DROP DEFAULT stores NULL. Fix (packages/drivers/driver-sql/** + 1 changeset): (1) MySQL drop_column_default on a nullable column runs SET DEFAULT NULL, NOT NULL keeps DROP DEFAULT (also covers the #4560 token arm). (2) A NOT NULL column with a stale literal DEFAULT and no declared default: the drop never travels alone. If the differ proposes relax_not_null (storage.notNull:false in words, or no storage declaration and not required, not the ceremony tenant column) the drop is emitted needs_confirm paired with it; publish and package install (#33724) select both when the field declares storage.notNull:false; os migrate apply applies both; afterwards an unset insert stores NULL on all three dialects. Otherwise (storage.notNull:true, required, ceremony column) the column is left alone and the entry is destructive, so it is warned at boot and listed by os migrate plan, never applied by a non-destructive door.
